edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Hom. in Cant. I, 10

source_text:
Equitatui meo in curribus Pharaonis assimilavi te. Si vis intellegere, o sponsa, quomodo scire te debeas, cognosce, cui te comparaverim, et tunc videbis talem te esse, quae turpari non debeas, cum tuam speciem recognoveris. Quid est igitur: Equitatui meo in curribus Pharaonis assimilavi te? Scio ego equitem sponsum propheta dicente: Et equitatio eius salus. Assimilata es ergo equitatui meo in curribus Pharaonis. Quanto differt equitatus meus, qui sum Dominus — equos eius et currus eius — quanto, inquam, differt equitatus meus ab equis Pharaonis, tanto tu melior es omnibus filiabus, tu sponsa, tu ecclesiastica anima, omnibus animabus, quae non sunt ecclesiasticae. Igitur si ecclesiastica anima es, omnibus animabus es melior. Deinde pulchritudinem sponsae spiritali amore describit: Genae tuae sicut turturis. Collum tuum sicut monilia.
Post haec fit sponsus in recubitu. Requievit quippe ut leo et ut catulus leonis obdormivit, ut deinceps possit audire: Quis suscitabit eum? Quo interim dormiente apparent sponsae sponsi sodales angeli et his eam sermonibus consolantur: Nos tibi aurea ornamenta facere non possumus; non sumus tam divites ut sponsus tuus, qui aureum tibi monile largitur; nos similitudines auri faciemus, non habemus aurum. Et hoc quoque laetandum est, si similitudines auri, si stigmata faciamus argenti. Similitudines auri faciemus tibi cum stigmatibus argenti, verum non omni tempore, sed donec sponsus tuus consurgat a cubitu. Si enim ille surrexerit, ipse tibi aurum, ipse faciet argentum, ipse tuam mentem sensumque decorabit, et eris vere dives in sponsi domo sponsa perfecta — cui gloria in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
pass_a_gloss: To cavalry of-me in chariots of-Pharaoh I-likened you. If you-wish to-understand how you-ought to-know yourself, learn to-whom I-compared you; then see you ought-not be-disfigured once you recognize your form. Prophet: And his riding is salvation. As far as my cavalry (I the Lord) differs from Pharaoh's horses, so far you bride / churchly soul better than all non-churchly souls. Then describes beauty: Cheeks yours as of-turtledove; neck yours as necklaces. After these the-bridegroom becomes on couch. He-rested indeed as lion and as cub of-lion he-fell-asleep, that thereafter he-may-be-able to-hear: Who will-raise him? With-whom meanwhile sleeping appear to-bride companions of-bridegroom angels and with-these-words console her: We to-you golden ornaments to-make are-not-able; we-are not so rich as your bridegroom who golden to-you necklace bestows; we likenesses of-gold we-will-make, we-do-not-have gold. And this also is-to-be-rejoiced, if likenesses of-gold, if stamps of-silver we-make. Likenesses of-gold we-will-make for-you with stamps of-silver, but not for-all time, but until your bridegroom rises from couch. If indeed that-one will-have-risen, he-himself for-you gold, he-himself will-make silver, he-himself your mind and-sense will-adorn, and you-will-be truly rich in bridegroom's house bride perfect — to-whom glory into ages of-ages. Amen.

pass_b_english: [[I have likened you to my cavalry among Pharaoh’s chariots >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:9]]. If you wish to understand, O Bride, how you ought to know yourself, learn to whom I have compared you, and then you will see that you are such as ought not to be disfigured, once you recognize your own beauty. What then is this: I have likened you to my cavalry among Pharaoh’s chariots? I know the Bridegroom as a rider, the prophet saying: [[And his riding is salvation >> Bible:Habakkuk 3:8]]. You have been likened, then, to my cavalry among Pharaoh’s chariots. As far as my cavalry differs — I who am the Lord, his horses and his chariots — as far, I say, as my cavalry differs from Pharaoh’s horses, so far are you better than all daughters, you the Bride, you the churchly soul, better than all souls that are not churchly. Therefore if you are a churchly soul, you are better than all souls. Then he describes the Bride’s beauty with spiritual love: [[Your cheeks are like a turtledove’s >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:10]]. Your neck is like necklaces. After this the Bridegroom is on his couch. For he rested and slept like a lion and like a lion’s cub, that afterward it might be asked: [[Who will raise him up? >> Bible:Numbers 24:9]]. While he sleeps, the Bridegroom’s companions — the angels — appear to the Bride and comfort her with these words: We cannot make you ornaments of gold; we are not so rich as your Bridegroom, who bestows on you a golden necklace; we will make likenesses of gold, for we have no gold. And even this is cause for joy, if we make likenesses of gold, if we fashion stamps of silver. [[We will make likenesses of gold for you with stamps of silver >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:11]], yet not for every time, but [[until your Bridegroom rises from his couch >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:12]]. For if he has risen, he himself will make gold for you, he himself will make silver, he himself will adorn your mind and sense, and you will be truly rich in the Bridegroom’s house as a perfect Bride — to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
